rule: Never collapse semantically different missing/invalid states into one null value.

values.UNKNOWN: Truth or value has not been established.
values.UNAVAILABLE: Required data, source, resource, or evidence cannot currently be accessed.
values.CONTRADICTORY: Two or more supported claims are mutually incompatible under the same declared scope/context.
values.NOT_APPLICABLE: The field or criterion does not semantically apply to this object or Sequence instance.
values.ABSENT: Evidence supports that the object/value/condition is not present.
values.UNDECLARED: The field is required by schema or workflow but has not yet been specified.
values.REDACTED: The value exists or is believed to exist but is intentionally withheld.
values.ERROR: Evaluation or retrieval failed, so no semantic value can be asserted from that operation.

machine_rules: UNAVAILABLE is not UNKNOWN if the source/resource is known but inaccessible.
CONTRADICTORY preserves all supported conflicting claims; do not average them.
NOT_APPLICABLE is a valid explicit terminal evaluation for a field/criterion.
UNDECLARED must block any transition whose contract requires the declaration.
ERROR describes an operation failure, not the truth value of the underlying claim.
